Shiny applications

Source: vignettes/shiny.Rmd
shiny.Rmd

Browse the Shiny gallery to open a standalone app, or run the examples here alongside their R source. The first launch downloads R and its dependencies. The apps use the highcharter version documented here.

Basics

Select Sepal or Petal. The same 150 flowers move to their new coordinates. Put highchartOutput("flowers") in the UI and read input$measure inside renderHighchart() to rebuild the plot when the measurement changes.

library(shiny)
library(highcharter)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("measure", "Iris measurements", c("Sepal", "Petal")),
  highchartOutput("flowers", height = "310px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$flowers <- renderHighchart({
    hchart(
      iris,
      "scatter",
      hcaes_string(
        x = paste0(input$measure, ".Length"),
        y = paste0(input$measure, ".Width"),
        group = "Species"
      )
    ) |>
      hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Length (cm)")) |>
      hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Width (cm)"))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Open the app in its own tab

Proxies

Start with twelve months of air passenger counts. Add a month appends one observation with hcpxy_add_point(). Columns changes the series type with hcpxy_update_series(). Switch back to Line and your added months are still there. Both controls target the series ID traffic through highchartProxy("passengers", session).

library(shiny)
library(highcharter)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("next_month", "Add a month"),
  radioButtons(
    "type",
    "Chart type",
    c("Line" = "line", "Columns" = "column"),
    inline = TRUE
  ),
  highchartOutput("passengers", height = "300px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  passengers <- as.numeric(AirPassengers)
  initial <- 12L
  output$passengers <- renderHighchart({
    highchart() |>
      hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Month since January 1949")) |>
      hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Passengers (thousands)")) |>
      hc_add_series(
        type = "line",
        id = "traffic",
        name = "Air passengers",
        pointStart = 1,
        data = passengers[seq_len(initial)]
      )
  })

  proxy <- highchartProxy("passengers", session)
  observeEvent(input$next_month, {
    i <- initial + input$next_month
    req(i <= length(passengers))
    hcpxy_add_point(proxy, id = "traffic", point = passengers[i])
  })
  observeEvent(
    input$type,
    {
      hcpxy_update_series(proxy, id = "traffic", type = input$type)
    },
    ignoreInit = TRUE
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Open the app in its own tab

To switch from weekly to daily Stock prices when the visible date range narrows, run the Stock proxy app or read the Stock walkthrough.

Events

Click a band in the equalizer. Shiny receives its ID at input$eq_point_click$pointid automatically. Drag the band and release it. The app uses only hc_add_event_point(event = "drop") to send the final gain in decibels to input$eq_point_drop$y.

library(shiny)
library(highcharter)

bands <- data.frame(
  band = c("60 Hz", "250 Hz", "1 kHz", "4 kHz", "16 kHz"),
  gain = c(0, 3, -2, 2, 0)
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  h2("Equalizer"),
  p("Click a band to select it. Drag it up or down to adjust its gain."),
  highchartOutput("eq", height = "320px"),
  textOutput("selected"),
  textOutput("adjusted")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$eq <- renderHighchart({
    hchart(
      bands,
      "scatter",
      hcaes(x = band, y = gain, id = band),
      name = "Gain",
      cursor = "ns-resize",
      lineWidth = 2,
      marker = list(enabled = TRUE, radius = 8),
      dragDrop = list(
        draggableY = TRUE,
        dragMinY = -12,
        dragMaxY = 12,
        dragPrecisionY = 1
      )
    ) |>
      hc_yAxis(
        min = -12,
        max = 12,
        tickInterval = 3,
        title = list(text = "Gain (dB)")
      ) |>
      hc_tooltip(valueSuffix = " dB") |>
      hc_add_event_point(event = "drop")
  })

  output$selected <- renderText({
    point <- req(input$eq_point_click)
    sprintf("Selected band: %s", point$pointid)
  })
  output$adjusted <- renderText({
    point <- req(input$eq_point_drop)
    sprintf("Last adjustment: %s at %+d dB", point$pointid, point$y)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Open the app in its own tab

The output ID, scope and case-sensitive Highcharts event name determine the input. For example, hc_add_event_series(event = "mouseOver") would send the hovered series to input$eq_series_mouseOver.

Linked views

Click a species in the overview to see the individual flowers in the detail chart. The server reads input$overview_point_click$pointid and uses a proxy to replace the detail series and its title. This combines the two preceding patterns and keeps both charts mounted.

library(shiny)
library(highcharter)

species <- aggregate(Petal.Length ~ Species, iris, mean)

ui <- fluidPage(
  p("Click a species to see its individual flowers."),
  fluidRow(
    column(5, highchartOutput("overview", height = "295px")),
    column(7, highchartOutput("detail", height = "295px"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$overview <- renderHighchart({
    hchart(
      species,
      "column",
      hcaes(x = Species, y = Petal.Length, id = Species),
      name = "Mean petal length",
      cursor = "pointer"
    ) |>
      hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Mean petal length (cm)"))
  })
  output$detail <- renderHighchart({
    hchart(
      subset(iris, Species == "setosa"),
      "scatter",
      hcaes(x = Petal.Length, y = Petal.Width),
      id = "flowers",
      name = "Flowers"
    ) |>
      hc_title(text = "setosa") |>
      hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Petal length (cm)")) |>
      hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Petal width (cm)"))
  })
  observeEvent(input$overview_point_click, {
    selected <- input$overview_point_click$pointid
    highchartProxy("detail", session) |>
      hcpxy_set_data(
        "scatter",
        iris[iris$Species == selected, ],
        hcaes(x = Petal.Length, y = Petal.Width),
        id = "flowers"
      ) |>
      hcpxy_update(title = list(text = selected))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Open the app in its own tab
